item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00085","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C06","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 is a highly plausible material drafting template. The child reproduces its two-recital structure, the distinctive statutory finding about a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in interstate and foreign commerce and producing goods for commerce, and the same three-part operative sequence governing the Board's powers, section 206 report, and continued existence. The principal changes adapt the template from bituminous coal to copper and other non-ferrous metals and update the parties and deadline. C06 and C09 employ substantially the same machinery, but C02 is closest in the phrasing of the factual finding, including disputes that have resulted or threaten to result in strikes or lockouts and the reference to occurrence or continuation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"such disputes have resulted, or threaten to result, in strikes or lockouts affecting a substantial part of the copper and non-ferrous metals industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce","parent_excerpt":"such dispute has resulted or threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce","explanation":"Distinctive language and syntax are retained while the number of disputes and the affected industry are changed."},{"child_excerpt":"which strikes or lockouts, if permitted to occur or continue, will imperil the national health and safety","parent_excerpt":"which strike or lockout, if permitted to occur or to continue, will imperil the national health and safety","explanation":"The child closely reproduces the statutory danger finding, with only grammatical changes for plural disputes."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before September fourth, 1951.
